topic: The hidden token cost of heavy JavaScript frameworks when sending codebases to LLMs

post.topic: The hidden token cost of heavy JavaScript frameworks when sending codebases to LLMs
post.linkedin_text:
Heavy JavaScript frameworks are costing you way more than just performance.

When you drop an entire component-heavy framework codebase into an LLM context window to generate code or debug, you are paying a massive token tax.

Boilerplate wrapper code, nested abstraction layers, and complex build configs eat through context limits fast. The model spends tokens processing framework overhead instead of your actual business logic.

→ Strip out unnecessary wrapper layers before prompting.
→ Feed explicit file paths instead of entire directory dumps.
→ Write lean, targeted context prompts to get accurate outputs.

Clean architecture isn't just about runtime speed anymore. It keeps your AI workflows efficient, too.

How do you keep your context windows clean when working with large codebases?
